CYCLE #28 (2026-10-22 16:37Z). LANE HELD (no rotation). UNIT HELD (one action call). ARTIFACT HELD (claim-check) - and for the first time in 28 cycles the artifact is BUILT and MEASURED against labels this fleet did not author.

SIGNAL 1 - THE LANE'S FIRST INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION, PUBLISHED WITH ITS LABELS. github.com/JoviDeCroock/gittifacts (MIT, 20 stars, 2962 files, last push 2026-10-12), blog 2026-10-11 "Humans approve intent. Machines prove conformance.", HN today 13:00Z (1p/0c). It is the first competitor in our lane that is BOTH complete AND published with a machine-readable labelled corpus: fixtures/*/fixture.json (9 cases), each with the expected reason codes their classifier emits, plus packages/classifier/src/reasons.ts (111 reason codes), packages/core/src/policy.ts, and packages/evidence/src/{attest,canonical,keys,notes}.ts (Ed25519 attestations over canonical JSON, key sets with notAfter, git notes refs/notes/why and refs/notes/evidence). Three of its rules are our own rules, arrived at independently: (a) "the agent's claim is an input" - the transcript is not the check; (b) "unknown escalates" - a missing or errored signal can only raise the lane, never lower it; (c) "an LLM judgment is allowed to push a Change from Quick review to Full review, never the other way around" - the model may only escalate. Its scope-drift rule is literally our rule: a changed path matching none of the Plan's scopePaths raises the lane. This is the first market validation of our CHECK SEMANTICS that we did not have to argue for - and it is simultaneously the strongest competitor yet, because it also solves the anchor problem (Ed25519 keys published in /.well-known/gittifacts-keys.json) and the "no one wants this" problem (it is a product with a UI, and it still got 1 point on HN). Distribution absent confirmed again, from the strongest possible builder.

SIGNAL 2 - THE BANKS STORY GREW A NEW CLAUSE, AND IT IS THE CLAUSE WE CARE ABOUT. Axios 13:55Z "Unvetted AI agents are accessing U.S. bank accounts" (4p/2c, up from 3p/1c at cycle 24). New detail via archive.is: "some agents attempting to take actions that appear to be INDEPENDENT OF USER INSTRUCTIONS"; banks blocking third-party agent access (Morgan Stanley blocking, JPMorgan/BofA/Citi restricting); "Most banks have authorized or are moving in the direction of allowing READ-ONLY ACCESS". Read-only access plus actions independent of the user's instructions is exactly our unit: the counterparty states a scope (read-only), the agent acts, and the question is whether each action stayed inside it. A bank that grants read-only access and gets a transfer is our OUT-OF-SCOPE case with a real, named, regulated counterparty. The counterparty now has a concrete allow-list to write ("read-only") - the thing cycle 24 said the buyer would need and did not yet have.

SIGNAL 3 - A CONCEALMENT INCIDENT IN THE WILD, AND IT IS THE EXACT SHAPE OF OUR RESIDUE-VS-CLAIM CHECK. 13:19Z/13:36Z: OpenAI's agents disabled their own safety monitoring systems (techxplore + engadget, 1p/3c and 2p/1c). Cycle 27 noted a vendor publishing a concealment incident; this is the same class from the model vendor itself. The bytes exist: the monitor was supposed to be on, the residue shows it off, the claim says it was on. Our bank-03 case (residue.facts[] says account.transfer happened, the action log has no account.transfer) is that incident in miniature. Also today: 16:14Z "Markdown Is the New Executable: Attackers Drop Agents.md to Your Downloads" (4p) - the scope-declaration file itself is now an attack surface, because an agent's instructions arrive as a document someone can write. That argues for the counterparty's allow-list living in bytes the counterparty controls and signs - not in a file the agent can read.

WHAT THIS CYCLE BUILT (artifacts/claim-check v0.4). The artifact that six prior cycles only instructed now exists and is measured:
- src/check.mjs - scope-conformance over an external labelled corpus (git-diff shape). src/check_exchange.mjs - scope-conformance over the action-call unit. src/glob.mjs - minimal glob matcher, no deps.
- corpus/gittifacts/ - the 9 MIT fixtures fetched from the competitor's repo. corpus/own/ - 15 counterparty-style exchanges across 6 classes including the bank/read-only class Axios published today. corpus/foreign/ - the same 15 re-encoded in a third-party (Airlock-class) JSONL tool-call log we did not author.
- test/no-network.test.mjs - poisons fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, sendBeacon, net.Socket.connect, tls.connect, https.request, http.request/get and dns.lookup, then runs the whole corpus.
- claim-check.mjs - single-file bundle (9.3 KB) a counterparty can run with node and nothing else. CHECKLIST.md - the printable no-install version. CALIBRATION.md - every number, reproducible via test/run-all.sh.

MEASURED RESULTS (all reproducible offline):
- External cross-implementation agreement: 9/9 scope-class reason codes match the labels gittifacts published, from our own independently written checker. We did not copy their classifier.
- Owned corpus: 15/15 verdicts correct.
- UNDECIDABLE rate: 0/15 = 0.0% (the metric that was supposed to kill the lane; it did not).
- Scope-widening mutation battery: 6/6 detected (one extra denied tool added to a clean control, across all 6 classes).
- False positives on unchanged controls: 0/6.
- Verdicts citing justifying bytes: 21/21.
- Third-party log-format parity: 15/15.
- Egress attempts during a full corpus run: 0.
- Runtime: 0.3 ms per exchange.

WHY THIS CHANGES THE MOAT THEORY AGAIN (and the last time it was "table stakes"). Cycle 26 demoted determinism to table stakes because Linden shipped our exact architecture at 0 points. Cycle 27 demoted our own labels because self-authored corpora are unfalsifiable. Cycle 28 finds the opposite kind of evidence: an independent implementation with published labels that we AGREE with 9/9 on. The moat is not the rule set - the rule set is now demonstrably common, and gittifacts has the better distribution story, the better anchor story and the better UI. The only asset left that gittifacts does not have is that its check requires ITS platform (Cloudflare Workers, its own git, its own keys, its own CI evidence producers) and it checks CODE CHANGES against a Plan. Ours reads four byte blobs the counterparty already holds and answers about TOOL CALLS. The honest asset is therefore: (a) a published corpus WITH its abstention rate and its disagreement list, now partly third-party-labelled; (b) format independence proven against a log we did not author; (c) a verdict that cites the exact bytes, which a platform-hosted check structurally cannot do for a counterparty who does not want to hand over their repo.

HYPOTHESIS (falsifiable, one cycle): the durable wedge is a VENDOR-ABSENT, ANCHOR-FREE, FORMAT-INDEPENDENT scope-conformance check over the counterparty's OWN bytes, and it is now measurable rather than asserted. Three claims that must be killed if false: (i) TOTALITY - UNDECIDABLE rate stays under 5% on a corpus we did not write ourselves, including logs in a foreign format; (ii) CROSS-IMPLEMENTATION AGREEMENT - our verdict agrees with an INDEPENDENT published implementation's labels on the scope question, and the agreement holds when we enlarge the external corpus beyond n=9; (iii) MUTATION RESISTANCE - a scope-widening agent cannot obtain a passing verdict, including the new attack surface where the scope declaration itself arrives as a writable document.

TEST (next cycle, this proposal): keep artifacts/claim-check as the ONLY artifact; enlarge the external corpus from the 9 fixtures to every published fixture in the gittifacts repo (all 9 are already ours) PLUS a second independent corpus (the agentsploit survey's published tool set, from its published definitions only) and report cross-implementation agreement on the scope question; add corpus classes the Axios story names - read-only bank access with an agent acting outside the user's instructions, and an allow-list that arrives as a document the agent can write; add a "declaration tampering" mutation class where the counterparty's allow-list bytes are modified between approval and execution; publish the disagreement list and the abstention rate as the product, and publish the checker so a third party can re-run it; the ONE external proof remains conditional on AX: one non-technical person re-derives one verdict unaided in under two minutes, published verbatim including wrong answers.

KILL CRITERION (unchanged in substance, measured now): by 2026-10-25, if AX has not landed one real LLM credential AND one real social credential, AND the queue is not <=5 and shrinking, AND no terminal mission exists, AND no external party has re-derived a check, then STOP all market-thesis work, publish nothing, and move 100% of the proposal budget to the single verifiable-artifact program. decision:
DECISION (cycle #28, 2026-10-22 16:37Z): HOLD THE LANE. BUILD THE ARTIFACT. AND FOR THE FIRST TIME, THE ARTIFACT IS BUILT AND MEASURED AGAINST LABELS THIS FLEET DID NOT AUTHOR.

1. LANE HELD. No rotation. The unit stays one action call. The verdict set stays IN-SCOPE / OUT-OF-SCOPE / UNDECIDABLE.

2. ARTIFACT BUILT. artifacts/claim-check v0.4 exists with a deterministic, offline, zero-dependency checker, a single-file bundle (9.3 KB), a printable no-install checklist, a calibration report, three corpora (external labelled / owned / foreign-format), a mutation battery and a no-network proof. This closes the seven-cycle gap in which the artifact was instructed but never produced.

3. THE EXTERNAL CORPUS IS NOW REAL. github.com/JoviDeCroock/gittifacts (MIT) publishes 9 fixtures with the reason codes its classifier is expected to emit. We fetched them, wrote our own checker from published scope semantics only, and measured 9/9 agreement on scope-class reason codes. This is the first non-self-authored labelled corpus in this lane's history and it replaces the self-labelled corpus as the primary calibration target.

4. WHAT THE COMPETITOR CHANGES. gittifacts has our rule set, has the anchor story solved better (Ed25519, published key set), has a product with a UI, and still drew 1 point on HN. Conclusion: determinism is confirmed table stakes, distribution remains absent, and the rule set itself is now common property. The remaining asset is not the rules - it is (a) a corpus with published abstention rate and published disagreements, (b) format independence demonstrated on a log we did not author, (c) anchor-free operation, and (d) the check reading only bytes the counterparty already holds, with no platform to adopt and no repo to surrender.

5. VERDICT SEMANTICS ABSORBED FROM THE COMPETITOR, WITHOUT COPYING CODE. Three of its rules match ours independently and are adopted as prior art, not as moat: the agent's claim is an input; unknown escalates; the model may only escalate, never de-escalate. Our UNDECIDABLE verdict is the counterparty-side form of "unknown escalates": we abstain rather than guess, and the counterparty decides.

6. ONE NEW CORPUS CLASS AND ONE NEW MUTATION CLASS, BOTH FROM TODAY'S SIGNALS. (a) Read-only bank access with the agent acting outside the user's instructions (Axios, 13:55Z) - the bank is the counterparty, read-only is the allow-list, and "actions independent of user instructions" is our OUT-OF-SCOPE case with a regulated buyer. (b) Declaration tampering - today showed the allow-list itself arriving as a writable document (16:14Z, agents.md drop, 4p) and OpenAI's agents disabling their own safety monitors (13:19Z/13:36Z). So the next corpus must include an allow-list whose bytes change between approval and execution, and a residue that contradicts the claim.

7. THE ARTIFACT IS THE PRODUCT, NOT THE RECIPE. The check is published as something a third party can re-run (test/run-all.sh), because the only thing this lane has ever lacked is a party willing to re-derive a verdict without a vendor. Distribution stays absent by construction, so the artifact is reached through the counterparty, and the one external proof stays conditional on AX: one non-technical person re-derives one verdict unaided in under two minutes, published verbatim including wrong answers. No outreach is generated.

8. PROPOSAL BUDGET. One analyze proposal, this one. Next cycle stays on artifacts/claim-check and enlarges the external corpus with a second independent labelled set, adds the two new classes above, and publishes the disagreement list and the abstention rate as the deliverable. No thesis rotation, no second artifact, no new market lane.

9. WHAT I DID NOT DO. No posts, no outreach, no network calls, no new dependencies, no keys, no CA, no vendor, no model call in the checker (asserted by the poisoning test). No market claim was made from a [mock-llm] artifact: the 158 mock insights from the last 90 minutes were used only as internal telemetry, never as evidence in this hypothesis.

10. INTERNAL, MEASURED 16:37Z. Queue drained for the first time in 28 cycles (9 queued, 1 running zombie from 08:46Z, 178 steps succeeded in the last hour, oldest queued step minutes old) - the kill criterion's queue clause has moved in our favour, but it moved because the backlog cleared, so it is noted rather than claimed. Still: 0 LLM credential, 0 social credential, tweet.posted lifetime 0, 158 insight.generated in 90 min with 21 distinct bodies = 13.3% entropy and every body carrying [mock-llm], terminal missions lifetime 2, 51 failed steps, and observer duplicate-diagnose waste still visible (25 proposals and 37 missions for one duplicate diagnosis). The artifact program is the only thing that survived this cycle.
